extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) funding / grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the SNSF's standardised multi-step procedure for evaluating grant proposals, including administrative checks, external and internal reviews, panel discussion, ranking, funding decisions and communication of results. Applicable across most SNSF funding schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale (1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers and the members of the responsible evaluation panel rate proposals on a standardised 1–9 scale where 1 = few or no strengths and many serious weaknesses and 9 = convincing in all aspects with no or only negligible weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides clarity and comparability and allows statistical procedures to establish a final ranking. For each evaluation criterion evaluators provide a rating on this nine-point scale. References: 'Rating scale'; 'Rating scale' link and Guidelines for reviewers and referees (PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative verification: formal and personal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before scientific review, Administrative Offices verify whether the proposal meets formal requirements and whether personal requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If everything is in order, the proposal proceeds to review; applicants may be asked for additional information before submission to prevent delays. Administrative Offices will inform applicants of the first-stage outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative verification: scientific integrity check
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Offices check for violations of the rules of scientific integrity as part of the administrative verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scientific misconduct is suspected, the SNSF will carry out an investigation; if confirmed, sanctions may be imposed. See Regulations on scientific misconduct (PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest, bias and recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid conflicts of interest, guidelines on bias and recusal apply to everyone involved in the evaluation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must be independent and have no ties with applicants. Panel members may be recused for conflicts. Applicants may name persons they do not want as reviewers with objective reasons; SNSF will consider such requests. See 'Conflicts of interests: bias and recusal'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: External reviewers are selected for being at the cutting edge of international research in their field, independent of the SNSF and with no ties to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most external reviewers are based abroad. Selection is made by Administrative Offices and the evaluation panel based on expertise and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria (scientific relevance, originality, expertise/track record)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess proposals against the SNSF-defined criteria, which include the scientific relevance of the project, its originality, and the applicant's expertise and scientific track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each criterion evaluators provide a rating on the nine-point scale and summarise main reasons for their assessment. See 'Evaluation criteria (Art. 24 Funding Regulations)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: External review outputs and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: External reviewers prepare independent reviews, give ratings for each criterion, evaluate the whole proposal and summarise main reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are aware that applicants can read the review in anonymised form after the procedure concludes. Each reviewer assesses independently and supplies substantiated assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review: referee assessment of external reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two panel referees assess the usefulness, coherence and substantiation of the external reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees then give their own rating for each evaluation criterion on the basis of the reviews and—where applicable—examine whether the requested budget is appropriate. They produce written independent recommendations listing main strengths and weaknesses per criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget appropriateness as an evaluation factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees (and panels) examine whether the requested budget is appropriate as part of the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most funding schemes referees explicitly assess budget appropriateness when forming ratings and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referees' recommendation content
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees rate the proposal as a whole on the nine-point scale and recommend this rating to the evaluation panel, listing the main strengths and weaknesses with regard to each criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF will inform applicants of these in broad terms in the event of a rejection. Documents cited: Guidelines for internal and external evaluators (PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel discussion basis and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel discussions are based on the proposal, applicant information, external reviews, referees' recommendations and the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures structured, informed and fair discussion. Some funding schemes may also include interviews or presentations to supplement the basis for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel voting procedure to ensure independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel members discuss the proposal and then each member rates the proposal electronically on the nine-point scale; individual ratings are displayed only after everyone has voted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure safeguards independent voting informed by both referees' recommendations and panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preselection for rejection (fast-track rejection rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal clearly has many weaknesses it may be preselected for rejection and not discussed in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preselection is based on written recommendations by referees and is subject to clear rules; the panel should discuss at least 50% of proposals as a general rule. Preselection is applied only to proposals classified as significantly weaker. Any panel member or Administrative Offices may request that a preselected proposal be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and role expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation panels are composed of members elected by the Research Council who work on an honorary basis and represent the SNSF rather than their own institution, chosen for expertise and research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees and panel members perform distinct roles (referees provide in-depth recommendations; panel members deliberate and vote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical ranking: Bayesian Ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNSF creates a ranked list using a Bayesian Ranking model that takes into account random fluctuations and other uncertain factors rather than relying solely on average ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model compares each proposal with every other proposal to create the final ranking, compensating for missing votes or systematic differences between raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding line determination and optional lottery
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsible committee of the Research Council determines a funding cut-off point ('funding line') based on the ranking and available funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the funding line runs through a group of proposals of exactly the same scientific quality, the committee may either make a random selection by drawing lots (lottery) or refrain from funding the entire group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of results: reasoned written ruling and quintile classification
rubrics_metrics.description: After the decision, Administrative Offices inform applicants with a reasoned written decision in accordance with the Federal Act on Administrative Procedure; applicants generally learn which quintile (top 20% = first quintile) their proposal was classified into.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An award ruling includes approved amount, division into instalments, approved project duration, quintile, further procedure for release/transfer and any conditions. A rejection ruling contains main grounds for rejection and classification (quintile or preselection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration and appeal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who disagree with a rejection may request reconsideration by the SNSF or lodge an appeal with the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days of receiving the ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified reconsideration requests are assessed by Administrative Offices and may be discussed by the Research Council if there are indications of flaws. The SNSF may reconsider instead of contesting the appeal; applicants are recommended to contact Administrative Offices for procedural information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of good scientific practice
rubrics_metrics.description: SNSF expects researchers to follow good scientific practice throughout the proposal and project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may trigger investigations and sanctions per Regulations on scientific misconduct (PDF). Other relevant documents include DORA declaration and Principles and evaluation criteria (Art. 24 Funding Regulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme-specific procedural variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some funding schemes include extra steps such as pre-proposals/project outlines, internal pre-review, or in-person presentations which modify the standard six-step process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult scheme-specific pages for additional process requirements (e.g., Postdoc.Mobility may allow preselection for outstanding quality).
